correctness.rationale: Translations of −S have barycentric upper caps z_i with Σ_i z_i=2; the S-intersection mass is an exact capped-simplex inclusion–exclusion sum. For nonnegative caps, Brunn–Minkowski gives concavity of the dth root of overlap mass; permutation symmetry of the remaining d caps makes the constrained maximizing vector (a,(2−a)/d,…). For 0<a<2/(d+1), lower/upper active facets make distinct cap polytopes nonhomothetic, giving strict growth along the path to equal caps and proving the cap-optimization step rather than relying on random tests. The maximum external barycentric coordinate L(y) controls the exclusion constraint, with saturation at c=2/(d+1). Dirichlet(1,…,1) barycentric mass gives exact H_d(u), so Dα consists of max λ_i≤uα, a reflected homothetic simplex; the vertex contact criterion u≤1/d, pointwise baseline atom mass β_d, and centroid max follow. An independent rational inclusion–exclusion check for d=3…8 and exact d=3 β=1/2, γ=5/8, contact=5/9 agrees. Exponential baseline estimate follows via independent Exp/Gamma representation and Chernoff bound. No finite sampling proves the d-uniform statements; the cap argument does.
residual_risks: Equality/strictness in Brunn–Minkowski is a critical nonstandard step: active lower/upper facets for 0<a<c were inspected as the needed nonhomothety witness.
The theorem requires K exactly the reflected same-size simplex and uniform base measure; other translations/dilations or nonuniform measures are not proven.

value.rationale: This determines the full ambient depth landscape, shape and support-contact of all upper regions, and the distribution of depth for a natural high-dimensional probability model under opposite-orientation convex translates. A surprisingly exact identity between baseline probability mass and depth level and explicit exponential concentration are mathematically motivated and potentially reusable in depth/statistics. The general-d theorem goes beyond the previously known planar special case, rather than an arbitrary finite parameter substitution.
residual_risks: No general dilations or nonuniform densities; broad natural extension remains unproved.

limitations: d≥3 new claim; d=2 and classical Dirichlet max formula are prior results.
